description: Forgotten Machines Museum builds an interactive digital museum that tells the stories of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. The project explores Apollo lunar hardware, retired Mars rovers and landers, and the Voyager spacecraft through interactive exhibits, a mission timeline, educational facts, and a quiz. The project helps visitors understand that space missions continue through their scientific discoveries and legacy.
summary:
SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital museum that preserves the stories of retired and forgotten space missions. It allows visitors to explore space equipment, mission timelines, historical facts, and interactive quizzes. The project addresses the challenge by making space history accessible, engaging, and easy to understand through a simple digital experience.

Visitors can open the website, choose a space exhibit, read its mission story, explore the timeline, discover facts, and take a quiz. This helps people understand that space missions continue through their discoveries, technology, and legacy, even after the mission ends.

SPACE RELICS is important because it preserves space history and inspires curiosity about science, technology, and space exploration. It shows how past missions still influence future discoveries and helps users appreciate the value of space equipment and research.

The website was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and hosted on GitHub Pages. It includes exhibit pages, mission stories, timelines, facts, and quizzes to create an engaging learning experience.
details:
SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital museum that preserves the stories of retired and forgotten space missions. It helps visitors understand that space missions continue through their discoveries, technology, and legacy.

The website allows users to explore different space exhibits, read mission stories, view timelines, discover important facts, and take interactive quizzes. Users can open the website, choose a space exhibit, learn about its purpose, and explore how the equipment contributed to space exploration.

The project benefits students, space enthusiasts, and general visitors by making space history easy to understand through a simple digital experience. It encourages curiosity about space exploration and helps people see the value of missions that are no longer active.

The intended impact is to preserve space history and inspire future interest in science, technology, and space exploration. SPACE RELICS was developed as a responsive website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. GitHub Pages was used to host the website. Google Gemini was used to assist with slide design and content generation.

The project is creative because it presents space equipment and mission history as an interactive digital museum. The team considered clarity, accessibility, simple navigation, engaging content, and educational value.
